_comment: Per-carrier front-end gain. The tuner is SINGLE-TENANT, so whichever
carrier we are on dictates the setting -- which makes the right gain a
property OF THE CARRIER, not a global constant. Two measurements on
2026-08-10 proved one setting cannot serve both: RF33 reads 0.0% FEC at
rfgain_sel 2 while an HDHomeRun on the same feed decodes at snq=100
(E73), and RF25 prefers 2 over 4 by +6.04 dB (E76).
Every entry records HOW it was measured, WHEN, and the number that
decided it, so a later reader can re-run the comparison instead of
trusting the value. An entry without provenance is a rumour.

why: For a carrier we have never measured, 4 is chosen on ASYMMETRY OF
HARM, not on preference. Measured worst cases: RF33 at 2 = TOTAL
loss (0.0% FEC, E73); RF25 at 4 = still decodes, just 6.04 dB
thinner (18.89 -> 12.85 dB, 6962 LDPC blocks converged and a
picture built from the g4 capture, E75/E76). So a wrong 4 costs
margin; a wrong 2 can cost the whole carrier. The old implicit
global default was 2, and that is exactly what produced E73's
total-loss surprise on the primary channel.
This is a placeholder, not a recommendation: run calibrate for any

8.method: NOT MEASURED -- single successful L1 decode, no A/B

metric.at_2: L1 decoded: FFT 8K, GI 768, Cred 0, SP4_2, 23 sym, 34.407 ms Frame, PLP0 QPSK 9/15 + PLP1 256QAM 9/15, HYBRID interleaver, not LDM

notes: rfgain_sel is deliberately null. ONE L1 at one gain is not an
A/B, and a later 190 s run did not reproduce it -- so there is
no value here honest enough to quote. Needs a proper
interleaved sweep (2/4/2/4, non-adjacent) before it earns one.
HAZARD, and the reason this entry exists at all rather than
being left absent: the DEFAULT IS 4, AND 4 IS THE VALUE THAT
FAILED HERE. An absent entry is not neutral -- lookup() would
hand RF8 the one setting we have evidence against, and the
failure would look like 'RF8 is undecodable' rather than 'we
tuned it wrong'. Any RF8 work must pass an EXPLICIT gain.
This also bounds the default's own justification. 'A wrong 4
costs margin; a wrong 2 can cost the whole carrier' was induced
from RF33 and RF25, both UHF and both strong. RF8 is VHF-high
at 183 MHz on the discone and inverts the asymmetry: here 4
cost everything and 2 was the one that worked. The default is
a UHF rule wearing a global name.
Antenna matters more than gain for this carrier: yagi pr 14.6
vs discone pr 56.6. The discone is RF8's antenna.

25.method: banked-capture A/B, 150 frames each, three minutes apart
antenna_caveat: E90: GAIN IS ANTENNA-SPECIFIC AND THIS VALUE IS NOT PORTABLE.
It was measured on the yagi, where RF25 is a weak carrier (peak
-12.6 dBFS at rfgain_sel 2, and 2 was chosen for the +6.05 dB of
margin it bought a signal that barely worked). On the Philips
(Antenna A) RF25 is a STRONG carrier -- 83.2 vs the yagi's 62.9
-- and it decoded live at 94.5% FEC. A setting picked to rescue
a starved feed is exactly the setting most likely to overload a
healthy one, which is the RF33-at-2 failure in mirror image.
No new value is asserted here: nothing has been measured on the
Philips. Anyone tuning RF25 on Antenna A must run their own A/B
and add a separate entry rather than inheriting this one.

headroom.note: does not overload at 2 -- it is a much weaker carrier

notes: RF25 = the WBFF multiplex (E94: WBFF is the HOST LICENSEE, not
a service name -- the carrier holds WNUV 54.1 on MMTP and
WBFFMob on ROUTE/DASH). Do not call this entry Fox. Both gains
decode; 2 buys 6.04 dB of margin.

33.method: live A/B on air, FEC percentage over ~14 samples per setting

headroom.note: strong local carrier; 2 overloads the front end totally

notes: REQUIRES 4. At 2 we read 0.0% FEC while an HDHomeRun on the same
feed decoded at snq=100 -- total, not marginal. 6 also reads
100.0%; 4 is seeded as the lower of the two that work.
Independent corroboration: the splitter A/B measured 100.0%
decodable at rfgain 4 vs 97.8% at 2 on the same feed.

30.method: capture decoded, but the gain used was NOT recorded
notes: RF30 DECODED, and at -21.0 dBFS it had real headroom -- but the
rfgain_sel in force during that capture was never written down,
so no value can honestly be seeded. rfgain_sel is deliberately
null: lookup() will fall back to the default AND report
measured=false. Populate with one A/B when the radio is free.
Recording the gain in the capture sidecar would have made this
entry free -- see E77 open items.

_comment: 8-VSB carriers seen by the HDHomeRun band scans of 8/08 and 8/10.
They are NOT decoded by this chain (it is an ATSC 3.0 receiver), so
no gain has ever been measured for them and none is invented here.
Listed so a future scan/tune path has somewhere to record one.
